title: Halting composition with a position bound
statement: Let $N$ and $M$ be nondeterministic Turing machines with Boolean symbols, respectively with $K$ and $K'$ work tapes and state sets $S$ and $S'$, on a fixed Boolean input. Let $\varphi$ map configurations of $N$ to configurations of $M$. Suppose that whenever a configuration $c$ of $N$ is nonhalting, one step of $M$ from $\varphi(c)$ under any choice bit equals the image under $\varphi$ of the corresponding step of $N$. Suppose there are natural numbers $m,B$ such that, from the image of any halting configuration $c$ whose input-head position is at most $B$, every choice word of length $m$ leads $M$ to a halting configuration. Then, for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and configuration $c$ of $N$ whose input-head position plus $n$ is at most $B$, if every choice word of length $n$ leads $N$ from $c$ to a halting configuration, every choice word of length $n+m$ leads $M$ from $\varphi(c)$ to a halting configuration.
